/PATCHSET_LEVEL.author: Ilya Nikolaevskiy
/PATCHSET_LEVEL.message:
The issue was the hardcoded test, expecting specific behavior from the GPU process as an evidence that hardware accelerated camera capture works end-to-end. 
That behavior was removed, but the test wasn't updated.

content/test/gpu/gpu_tests/trace_integra.author: Ilya Nikolaevskiy
content/test/gpu/gpu_tests/trace_integra.message:
This happens when the texture frame is being converted/mapped for software encoding. I'm not sure if this is the correct one. We want something to show evidence that the GPU process will try to render the texture frame without falling back to something different.

I think something from the D3D_image_backing is more appropriate here, but I'm not sure.

content/test/gpu/gpu_tests/trace_integra.author: Ilya Nikolaevskiy
content/test/gpu/gpu_tests/trace_integra.message: Sorry, didn't notice that you've added this event yourself. But you've added it in the capture, and that's already covered in _MFD3D11VC_CAPTURE_EVENT_NAME. This PRESENT_EVENT_NAME is supposed to cover something in the GPU process while rendering the texture.

content/test/gpu/gpu_tests/trace_integra.author: Shaobo Yan
content/test/gpu/gpu_tests/trace_integra.message: Ah, I didn't noticed that CAPTURE_EVENT_NAME. Thanks for pointing it out. So do you think we could remove the `_MFD3D11VC_PRESENT_EVENT_NAME ` ? Because the logic is that we try to handle sync in capture process and then pass the frame to GPU process. So it shouldn't have any events.

content/test/gpu/gpu_tests/trace_integra.author: Ilya Nikolaevskiy
content/test/gpu/gpu_tests/trace_integra.message: No, I don't think we should remove it. We just have to use something other than KeyedMutex events. It's not checking that the image is synchronized. It tests that image is being presented, i.e. rendered. I suggest adding some event in d3d_image_backing, but I don't know what there is called when the image is rendered.
